name: Wbcom Designs – Private Community for BuddyPress
author: wbcomdesigns

sections.description:
Turn your BuddyPress site into an exclusive private community in minutes!

Private Community turns your BuddyPress site into a members-only space. Whether you are building a company intranet, a paid membership site, or a private group, you decide exactly who can see what.

Protection covers every surface a visitor can reach: pages, BuddyPress components, site search, the REST API, RSS feeds and XML sitemaps. If a logged-out visitor cannot open a page, they cannot find its title in search or pull it from an API either.

🎯 Perfect For:
• Company intranets and team portals
• Paid membership communities
• Private family or group websites
• Educational course platforms
• Exclusive member networks

🔒 Two Simple Protection Modes:

1. Partial Protection – Keep some areas public
• Lock specific member directories or group pages
• Protect certain URLs while keeping others open
• Use wildcards to protect entire sections (like /premium/*)

2. Full Protection – Lock everything except what you choose
• Make your entire site members-only
• Whitelist specific pages for public access
• Perfect for private company sites

⚙️ How Your Visitors See It:
• Built-in Login – Beautiful login form that matches your theme
• Custom Forms – Use your favorite form plugin
• Smart Redirect – Send visitors to a specific welcome page

💪 Why Choose Private Community?
• Set up in 2 minutes – No complicated configurations
• Works with any theme – Tested with popular BuddyPress themes
• Locks every surface – Pages, BuddyPress components, the REST API, feeds, XML sitemaps and site search, so protected content stays out of search results and syndication
• Built for large sites – No unbounded page queries, so protection costs the same on 50 pages or 5,000
• Secure by default – Blocks brute force attacks automatically
• Always compatible – Regular updates for latest WordPress versions

Documentation

📚 Comprehensive Documentation Available:

• Documentation – Setup guides, settings reference, URL rule syntax and troubleshooting
• Support – Ask us directly

sections.installation:
Quick Setup (2 minutes):

  1. Upload the plugin to your /wp-content/plugins/ directory
  2. Activate ‘Private Community for BuddyPress’ in your Plugins menu
  3. Go to WB Plugins → Private Community in the WordPress admin sidebar
  4. Choose your protection mode and save

That’s it! Your private community is ready.
sections.faq:
Do I need BuddyPress to use this plugin?

Yes. This plugin works with BuddyPress only. It needs BuddyPress installed and active, and it does not run on BuddyBoss Platform, which has its own private network setting.

How quickly can I set this up?

Most users have their private community running in under 2 minutes. Just choose your protection mode and you’re done!

Can I keep some pages public while protecting others?

Absolutely! Use Partial Protection mode to choose exactly which pages to protect, or use Full Protection with a whitelist for public pages.

Will this slow down my site?

No. Protection is decided by matching the requested URL against your rules, so the cost does not grow with the size of your site. The plugin runs no unbounded page queries.

Does protected content stay out of search results, feeds and the REST API?

Yes. A page you have locked is removed from site search results, RSS feeds, XML sitemaps and REST API lists, and opening it through the REST API is refused. BuddyPress activity feeds close when Activity, or the member or group they belong to, is locked. Full Protection blocks the REST API, every RSS feed and the XML sitemaps for logged-out visitors. If a visitor cannot open a page, they cannot find its title or content anywhere else either.

How exactly do URL rules match?

A rule matches the exact path or anything directly beneath it: /about covers /about and /about/team, but not /about-us. Use * for a whole section, for example /premium/*. The same rules apply to both the locked list and the public whitelist.

Can members still register if my site is locked?

Yes! The registration page can be whitelisted so new members can still sign up while the rest of your site remains private.

Does it work with my theme?

Private Community works with any properly coded WordPress theme. It’s been tested with all major BuddyPress themes.

What happens when non-members try to access protected content?

You choose! Show them a login form, redirect to a specific page, or display a custom message using any shortcode.

Is there a limit to how many pages I can protect?

No. Protect one page or your entire site. Before 2.4.0 slug matching quietly stopped working above 1,000 locked pages; that cap is gone.
sections.changelog:
2.4.0 – November 2026

Security release. Locked content no longer leaks through search, the REST API, RSS feeds or sitemaps, and a whitelist entry no longer un-protects unrelated pages. Everyone on 2.3.x or earlier should update.

  • New – The Partial Protection tab now warns you when Full Protection is on and its rules are not being applied, and confirms your settings are still saved.
  • Improve – Removed the silent 1,000-page cap that stopped slug matching on large sites.
  • Improve – The redirect-page picker and the add-all-pages tool no longer query every published page, and no longer issue one query per page. Both limits are filterable.
  • Improve – Locked-page filtering runs only on search, feed, REST and sitemap queries. It previously ran on every query on the site and discarded the result.
  • Improve – Pages locked by ID in old versions are turned into Protected URL rules once, on update, and the settings migrations no longer run on every page load.
  • Improve – The login form on the members-only screen is a real form: Enter logs you in, password managers fill it, and you return to the page you asked for, including through the sign in link.
  • Improve – The members-only screen’s Create an account link opens the BuddyPress registration page, so activation emails, required profile fields and anti-spam or captcha checks all apply. The in-place Register tab that skipped them is gone.
  • Fix – Pages chosen in the old Pages list (versions before 2.0) are moved to Protected URLs when you update, so they are locked again; recent versions had left them public.
  • Fix – Saving the Partial Protection tab no longer switches Full Protection off.
  • Fix – Locking Groups or Activity no longer locks members whose username contains “groups” or “activity”, and locking Members no longer locks a group’s Members tab.
  • Fix – The members-only screen no longer shows the locked member’s or page’s name in the browser tab title.
  • Fix – Upgrades from pre-2.0 no longer lose the locked-page list. The migration wrote it to the wrong option, and the runtime read a key that was never populated. Misplaced lists are recovered automatically.
  • Fix – Stopped defining BuddyPress’s BP_ENABLE_MULTIBLOG and BP_ROOT_BLOG constants, which pinned multisite installs to root blog 1 with multiblog disabled.
  • Fix – Settings screens no longer misread a missing settings record as a value, which could cause notices on a fresh install.
  • Fix – Corrected the installation instructions, which pointed to Settings instead of WB Plugins, and the documentation links, which returned 404 for everyone.
  • Fix – The members-only login screen now uses your theme’s colours in light and dark mode on BuddyX, BuddyX Pro and Reign, and its messages use the standard BuddyPress notice style.
  • Fix – Protecting a page now works even when that page is also saved as the redirect page; it stayed public under Show Login Form and Show Custom Content.
  • Fix – Removed the Share Feedback link from the Welcome tab, because the page it pointed to no longer exists.
  • Fix – Renamed an admin template file whose name made some hosting firewalls block the plugin upload.
  • Fix – The members-only screen no longer shows the locked page’s text in its meta description (Yoast SEO and Rank Math) or its title in a comments feed link or member and group activity RSS feed link, so search snippets and chat previews stay neutral.
  • Security – Pages locked with Protected URLs are no longer readable through the REST API, REST lists, RSS feeds or XML sitemaps.
  • Security – BuddyPress activity RSS feeds (site-wide, member, group, favorites and mentions) are now blocked for logged-out visitors when Activity, Members or Groups is locked, and always under Full Protection.
  • Security – With Site Wide Activity locked, logged-out visitors no longer see activity on group pages, profiles or widgets.
  • Security – The users sitemap is closed while Members is locked.
  • Security – Failed lock-screen logins are counted per visitor IP and username, so nobody can lock a member out from elsewhere, and the login request now always requires a valid security token.
  • Security – Locked pages are now removed from site search results. Locked URLs were resolved by comparing a full path against a page slug, so no nested page ever matched and wildcard rules were skipped entirely. A locked page kept its title, URL and excerpt in search results for logged-out visitors even though opening it was correctly blocked.
  • Security – Whitelist entries now match on path boundaries instead of substrings. Whitelisting “secret” also made “/secret-area/payroll/” public, and a one-letter entry exposed the whole site.
  • Security – A whitelist entry of “/” no longer un-protects your XML sitemap or feeds. WordPress treats sitemap requests as the front page, so under Full Protection the front-page rule exposed /wp-sitemap.xml.
  • Security – Locking a page by ID no longer also locks unrelated pages whose URL happens to contain its slug, so locking “about” no longer locks “/about-us-blog/”.
  • Security – On a fresh install the Partial Protection tab showed no components ticked while the site actually locked members, groups and activity. The tab and the site now read the same setting.
  • Security – The members-only screen no longer names the hidden member, group or page in shared link previews: Activity Share, Yoast SEO and Rank Math social tags and schema are turned off there, and the screen is marked noindex.
  • Security – Added the missing direct-access guards to five PHP files.
  • Dev – Requires PHP 8.1. Removed the Grunt build, the WordPress Plugin Boilerplate loader and core classes, the Bp_Lock_Globals class and the $bplock global, the review notice, the Discover tab, the uninstall stub, Font Awesome (about 1 MB) and the lock-screen Register tab with its bplock_register AJAX action, bp_lock_after_register_form action and bplock_register_success_message filter. Releases are built with bin/build-release.sh and translations with wp i18n make-pot.
  • Dev – Lock decisions for templates, search, REST, feeds and sitemaps now share one check, and component locks follow BuddyPress routing instead of matching URL text.
  • Dev – Added bplock_filter_search_results, bplock_get_all_pages_limit and bplock_redirect_page_limit filters.
  • Dev – All allow and deny matching now runs through one Bp_Lock_Url_Matcher class so the two lists cannot drift apart again.
  • Dev – The add-all-pages AJAX response is now an object with urls, truncated and limit. The previous bare array is still accepted by the bundled script.
  • Compat – Tested up to WordPress 7.1.

2.3.1 – July 2026

Security release. The private-community lock now also covers the REST API, feeds, and XML sitemaps, which previously stayed readable to logged-out visitors.

  • Security – Blocked the REST API for logged-out visitors while the lock is active. Full Protection blocks every route except the login allowlist; Partial Protection blocks the BuddyPress namespace and user enumeration when a component is locked.
  • Security – Blocked feeds and XML sitemaps for logged-out visitors under Full Protection so private content is no longer syndicated or enumerated.
  • Security – Hardened partial-mode URL locking so a locked page cannot be reached through its ?page_id= or ?p= query URL.
  • Dev – Added bplock_rest_allowed_routes, bplock_restrict_rest_route, and bplock_restrict_feeds filters to tune the new enforcement.
  • Compat – Declared Requires PHP 7.4 and Requires Plugins: buddypress in the plugin headers.
